  DESIGN AND IMPLEMENTATION OF HUMAN-COMPUTER INTERFACES [NPT-4008]  
  Marks: 50                                                                              Duration: 180 mins.  
  PART-A  
  Answer all the questions.  
  1)           Which input and output devices would you select for the following systems?  
  
  i) tractor-mounted crop-spraying controller  
  A)      ii) air traffic control system                                                            (5)  
  
  For each device, evaluate the alternatives and highlight any relevant reasons why  
  traditional options like the keyboard, mouse, and CRT monitor might be less ideal.  
  
  B)      What is the goal and importance of human computer interface. Why human computer  
  interface development is multidisciplinary? Discuss.                                      (5)  
  
  2)           How do you apply the following interaction styles in the interface development of the  
  bus ticket booking system? Explain.  
  a) Menus b) Form fills                                                                    (5)  
  A)      Discuss their benefits and drawbacks in HCI.  
  
  B)      In a scenario, a single CPU is utilized by various users to execute the tasks they submit  
  via an interface. Which paradigm is most appropriate for this situation? Please elaborate (5)  
  on the chosen paradigm, highlighting its benefits and drawbacks.  
  
  3)           Explain in detail Shneiderman's golden rules for effective design of human computer  
  interface  
  (5)  
  A)  
  B)      Compare and contrast waterfall model and prototyping model for software development.  
  How do you incorporate HCI usability factor in these models?                         (5)  
  
  4)           Explain the different goals of evaluation. Why it is important to apply evaluation  
  techniques for HCI design? Discuss  
  (5)  
  A)  
  B)      Discuss the different requirements of user support in HCI systems. Give any three  
  examples of user support.                                                                 (5)

  However, organizational issues can break or make a system. Justify this statement with
